assessments.topic: 1987 partially purified NadK preparation and assay contexts
assessments.summary: The unspecified K12, glycerol-grown, 93-fold enriched and explicitly nonhomogeneous preparation remains distinct from the 2001 preparation and modern MG1655 reference. General Methods used 10 mM NAD and ATP; Table 2 changed NAD to 4.0 mM; separate saturation curves varied NAD. The complete K87 ledger retains all other preparation, exact endpoint-qualifier links and typed comparator links unchanged.

The accepted paragraph assigns the Table 2 inhibition/additivity comparison to 4.0 mM NAD and the NADPH 5–30 µM / NADH 50–200 µM series to variable-NAD saturation experiments. General assay conditions, Hill ranges, binding-site inference limits and the abstract/Results Km discrepancy remain explicit.
assessments.details: The 1987 NadK preparation came from an unspecified E. coli K12 substrain grown in forced-aerated glycerol minimal medium at37°C and harvested in late log phase. It was enriched93-fold and was explicitly not homogeneous. The general assay used 10 mM NAD and 10 mM ATP, 14 mM MgCl2 and 100 mM MOPS at pH 7.2. Table 2 instead used 4.0 mM NAD, found that roughly tenfold more NADH than NADPH was needed for similar inhibition, and reported additive inhibition when both were present. Separate saturation experiments varied NAD, using NADPH at 5–30 µM or NADH at 50–200 µM. NAD saturation became sigmoidal, with reported Hill coefficients1.8–2.1 for NADPH and1.7–2.0 for NADH; increasing NAD could overcome inhibition. These kinetic observations and native allosteric annotations do not locate a binding site experimentally. The abstract assigns Km1.9 mM to NAD and2.1 mM to ATP, whereas the Results reverse those assignments; both are retained as an internal discrepancy.
